newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NO HANGOVER FOR UNITED IN GOODISON SUNSHINE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO HANGOVER FOR UNITED IN GOODISON SUNSHINE.

text.p: Manchester United showed no signs of a hangover from their visit to Porto when they beat Everton 2-0 at Goodison Park on Saturday to open up a six-point lead at the top of the English premier league.

United had failed to win in the league immediately after their last five matches in the European Cup but they were never seriously troubled by a pedestrian Everton side who were always second-best in the spring sunshine.
The home team were not helped by reserve goalkeeper Paul Gerrard making errors for both goals.

He was slow to get down to Ole Solskjaer's 35th-minute opener and then completely missed the the ball when he came out to cut out a cross which Eric Cantona converted for United's second after 79 minutes.

United had lost only twice at Goodison in the last eight seasons and, while never playing at their best following their European Cup quarter-final success over Porto, they were always too good for the home side.

Duncan Ferguson, who had never previously been on the losing side against United, lost that record but was lucky to stay on the pitch after appearing to elbow David May in the face in the first half which earned him only a yellow card.
United moved on to 63 points with seven matches to play. Second-placed Arsenal meet third-placed Liverpool at Highbury on Monday. Both have 57 points.
Most interest on Saturday was focused on the bottom end of the table.

Middlesbrough, who had not lost at home to Chelsea since 1931, maintained that record with a 1-0 victory thanks to a second-half goal from Brazilian Juninho, who has scored four times in the last five matches.
The match, a possible F.A. Cup Final rehearsal, produced Middlesbrough's fourth successive league win and took them out of the bottom three for the first time since December.

Their position will be even healthier if an inquiry next Wednesday decides to restore the three points deducted from their total in January after they refused to play a match at Blackburn because of injuries and illness.
West Ham also boosted their chances of avoiding the drop with a 3-1 win at fellow strugglers Coventry who slipped back into the relegation zone for the first time since December.

Coventry, who have never been relegated since they moved up to the top division in 1967, scored first through Dion Dublin but two goals from John Hartson and one from Les Ferdinand's young cousin Rio Ferdinand, gave the Hammers the points.
"It was an important match and one that we could not afford to lose," Hammers manager Harry Redknapp said.
It was also a good afternoon for worried Derby who had slipped into the relegation dog-fight after winning just two of their last 15 league matches.

They raced into a 2-0 lead against Tottenham after only 22 minutes through Robbie van der Laan and Paul Trollope but Spurs fought back with goals from substitute Ronny Rosenthal (29) -- his first in the league for three years -- and Jason Dozzell (50).
Derby then regained the initiative with two goals in two minutes from Dean Sturridge (68) and substitute Ashley Ward (69) to win 4-2.

Former England international Chris Waddle made his debut for Sunderland, the team he supported as a boy, but could not inspire them to victory against fellow strugglers Nottingham Forest, the team which almost signed him from Bradford last week.
Kevin Ball scored from a Waddle corner to put Sunderland ahead after 61 minutes but Des Lyttle saved a point for lowly Forest with an 86th-minute equaliser.
Southampton stayed bottom after being held to a 2-2 draw at home by Leicester, who came back twice to save a point.

Norwegian striker Egil Ostenstad put the Saints ahead after 32 minutes and Emile Heskey scored Leicester's first equaliser a minute after halftime. Two minutes after that Dutch defender Ulrich van Gobbel made it 2-1 to the home side but Leicester got a share of the points when Steve Claridge equalised after 70 minutes.
